title: Observability: dashboards + alerts for retention enforcement (lag, throughput, errors, storage growth)
creator: Sean Gallagher
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation (Retention controls + compliance reporting pack)
description:
Context
Retention controls are rolling out across audit logs + selected telemetry/analytics datasets. To make enforcement provable and safe for enterprise workloads, we need first-class observability for retention enforcement workers and datastore health.

This ticket covers:
1) Dashboards to visualize enforcement lag, throughput, error rates, and storage growth risk.
2) Alerting with actionable thresholds, paging policies, and guardrails to avoid false positives during backfills/canaries.

Goals / success criteria
- SRE and oncall can answer within 2 minutes:
  - Is retention enforcement running for a tenant/env/region?
  - Are we within retention SLO (no material lag)?
  - Are deletes failing or being rate-limited?
  - Are datastores growing in a way that implies enforcement is stuck?
- Alerts fire before customer impact (e.g., storage bloat risk, retention lag > threshold), include runbook links, and are scoped so we don’t page for expected pauses.

In scope
- Metrics + dashboards for:
  - audit-log retention enforcement worker (ENG-2920)
  - telemetry/analytics TTL enforcement (ENG-2921)
- Alert policies for:
  - enforcement lag (by dataset/env/region)
  - delete/TTL error rate
  - throughput drop to ~0 (stuck worker) when lag exists
  - storage growth / bloat indicators (table/partition size growth against baseline)
- Runbook integration: alerts must deep-link to the retention enforcement job runbook and dashboard panels.

Out of scope
- Building a customer-facing Console dashboard (this is internal SRE/eng tooling).
- Adding per-request payload inspection or logging of sensitive data.

Implementation notes
Dashboards (Grafana)
Create/extend a “Retention Enforcement” dashboard (folder: Security & Compliance) with the following panels and drilldowns:

A) Enforcement health (overview)
- Last successful run time by dataset + region + environment
- Current enforcement lag (hours) by dataset + region (top-N + heatmap)
- Worker queue depth / backlog (if applicable)

B) Throughput + performance
- Delete throughput: rows/sec and/or bytes/sec (stacked by dataset)
- Job duration p50/p95
- Batch sizes and rate-limit activity (to correlate with elevated DB load)

C) Errors + retries
- Error rate by error_code (permission, timeout, throttled, invariant violations)
- Retries and dead-letter / skipped partitions counts

D) Storage growth / bloat risk
- Table size (bytes) and growth slope per day
- Partition count growth (where available)
- Correlate storage growth with lag to distinguish organic growth vs stuck enforcement

Metrics
Ensure these time series exist and are consistently labeled across enforcement components:
- retention_enforcement_last_success_timestamp{dataset,region,env}
- retention_enforcement_lag_seconds{dataset,region,env}
- retention_enforcement_deleted_rows_total{dataset,region,env}
- retention_enforcement_deleted_bytes_total{dataset,region,env} (if available)
- retention_enforcement_errors_total{dataset,region,env,error_code}
- retention_enforcement_job_duration_seconds_bucket{dataset,region,env}
- retention_enforcement_backlog_count{dataset,region,env} (if there is a backlog concept)

Notes:
- For telemetry TTL (partition expiry), “deleted_rows_total” may be approximated; at minimum expose a ‘partitions_expired_total’ counter and a ‘ttl_application_errors_total’ counter.
- Labels must NOT include tenant_id for cardinality. We can include “tier” and/or “deployment_mode” where safe. Tenant-specific debugging should be via ad-hoc logs/traces and support tooling.

Alerting
Create the following alerts (Datadog monitor or Prometheus alertmanager, consistent with existing SRE standards):

1) Retention enforcement lag high (page)
- Condition: retention_enforcement_lag_seconds > 24h for audit logs in production, sustained 30m
- Routing: #oncall-sre (page), with secondary notification to #eng-security
- Message must include:
  - affected dataset/region/env
  - link to dashboard panel
  - first-step runbook actions

2) Retention enforcement lag elevated (ticket)
- Condition: lag > 6h sustained 60m
- Routing: create incident ticket / slack notify without paging

3) Delete error rate high (page)
- Condition: errors_total rate > 1% of delete ops for 15m OR any “invariant” error_code > 0 sustained 5m

4) Stuck worker / zero throughput while lag exists (page)
- Condition: deleted_rows_total rate ~0 for 30m AND lag > 6h

5) Storage growth anomaly (ticket -> page if severe)
- Condition: table_size_bytes slope exceeds baseline by >X% for 24h OR size crosses defined budget threshold for the datastore
- Note: tune thresholds separately for audit logs vs telemetry

Guardrails
- Alerts must be disabled or “no data = OK” during:
  - initial backfill windows (explicit maintenance window annotation)
  - canary rollout where enforcement is intentionally paused
- Add a dashboard annotation stream for retention releases (from #eng-releases) so oncall can correlate changes.

References
- SRE monitoring plan: Confluence /eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/monitoring-for-retention-enforcement
- Runbook: Confluence /eng-platform/runbooks/retention-enforcement-job-runbook
- Related implementation:
  - ENG-2920 (audit log enforcement worker)
  - ENG-2921 (telemetry TTL)

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Grafana dashboard exists with panels listed above and is discoverable under Security & Compliance.
- [x] Alerts created with correct routing + links to runbook and dashboard.
- [x] Thresholds reviewed by SRE (Sean) and Security Eng (Kevin) for reasonableness.
- [x] Cardinality review complete (no tenant_id labels).
- [x] Documented in runbook: where to look first, how to confirm false positive, and how to silence during maintenance.

Rollout plan
- Ship dashboards first (no alerts) for 48 hours to observe baseline.
- Enable ticket-level alerts.
- Enable paging alerts per dataset in phases (audit logs first, then telemetry TTL) after thresholds tuned.

Risks
- Elevated DB load if alerts prompt operators to “rerun now” too aggressively; runbook must emphasize rate limits and safe retry behavior.
- False positives during canary or partial-region rollout; mitigated with annotations + silences.
